sections.label: The legacy — Why Carlson Gracie

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: Carlson Gracie is one of the most important names in the history of Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu. We brought it to the Southern Lakes, and training here puts you in a direct line to the family that founded the sport.

texts.label: Photo caption
texts.value: Everyone has a hand in someone else’s journey.

texts.label: The lineage — description
texts.value: The art passed from Mitsuyo Maeda to Carlos Gracie, and from Carlos to his son Carlson. Carlson defended the family name for two decades without losing, then became one of the finest coaches the sport has produced. Our head professor, Jose Gomes, earned his black belt under Carlson Gracie Jr, so that line runs unbroken onto our mats.

texts.label: The standard — description
texts.value: Plenty of gyms teach jiu-jitsu. Few carry this much rank. With more than 11 black belts training regularly at our dojo, alongside a deep bench of high belts, you’ll be hard pressed to find deeper skill and knowledge anywhere in the country.

texts.label: The culture — description
texts.value: Carlson opened his mats to everyone and built teams instead of guarding secrets. That is the culture we keep: higher belts lift the newer ones, and everyone has a hand in someone else’s journey. Family-first and everyone-welcome, every single day.

sections.label: Good to know — Questions, answered

texts.label: What should I bring to my first class? — question
texts.value: What should I bring to my first class?

texts.label: What should I bring to my first class? — answer
texts.value: Shorts and a t-shirt are fine. We have clean gis to borrow, so there is nothing to buy before you know you love it. Bring water, a towel, and no ego.

texts.label: What makes Carlson Gracie different? — question
What makes Carlson Gracie different? — answer
texts.value: A few things you won’t find together anywhere else in the region. A direct line to the founding Gracie family, through our head professor’s black belt under Carlson Gracie Jr. A deep roster of black belts on the mat, more than 11 in all. And a family of academies across the South Island, in Queenstown, Wānaka, Invercargill and South Canterbury. We were the first to bring the sport to the Southern Lakes, and we have grown it ever since.

texts.label: Do I need to be fit to start? — question
texts.value: Do I need to be fit to start?

texts.label: Do I need to be fit to start? — answer
texts.value: No. You get fit by training, not before it. Every class runs at the pace your body sets, and nobody in the room is watching you.

texts.label: I have never done a martial art. Is that ok? — question
texts.value: I have never done a martial art. Is that ok?

texts.label: I have never done a martial art. Is that ok? — answer
texts.value: That describes most people’s first class here. Fundamentals exists for exactly this: basic positions, submissions and escapes, and the habits that keep you safe before you join the regular classes.

texts.label: How do I become a member? — question
texts.value: How do I become a member?

texts.label: How do I become a member? — answer
texts.value: Start with a free class, then have a chat with us on the mat. Membership covers your classes, the seminars we host, and the full tutorial library in the app.

texts.label: What ages are the kids’ classes? — question
texts.value: What ages are the kids’ classes?

texts.label: What ages are the kids’ classes? — answer
texts.value: Ages 5 to 12, in gi and no-gi. Games first, technique always, and no striking, ever.

texts.label: Gi or no-gi, which should I pick? — question
texts.value: Gi or no-gi, which should I pick?

texts.label: Gi or no-gi, which should I pick? — answer
texts.value: Either, and most members end up doing both. Gi is the traditional kimono and rewards patience and grips. No-gi is faster, closer to wrestling, and a little less to learn on day one.

title: about / our method
seoTitle: How We Teach | Our Method | Carlson Gracie NZ
seoDescription: Every academy teaches differently. Ours comes down to three things: tradition, strong foundations taught in blocks, and a culture that carries you.

sections.label: Top of page — Our method — How we teach

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: People think all jiu-jitsu is the same. Walk into three gyms and you’ll find out fast that it isn’t. Every academy teaches differently, whether they’ve ever said so out loud or not. Here’s ours, and it comes down to three things.

images.label: Photo
images.alt: A coach demonstrating a gi technique with students on the mats

sections.label: The Carlson Gracie standard — It comes down to three things

texts.label: Heading
texts.value: It comes down to three things

texts.label: Photo caption
texts.value: Technique is taught slowly. Learning happens together.

texts.label: Tradition — description
texts.value: We’re Carlson Gracie, right down to the warm-up. We run the mats, we line up, and we show respect to each other and to the room. We’re not precious about it. You won’t get told off for the wrong colour gi. But that old-school respect is what turns a room full of strangers into a proper academy.

texts.label: Strong foundations, taught in blocks — heading
Strong foundations, taught in blocks — description
texts.value: We don’t chase whatever’s trendy this year. We build deep foundations and teach in blocks, one idea at a time over a few weeks, so it actually lands. And we roll every single session. You can watch a hundred videos, but you get good by doing.

texts.label: Culture that carries you — description
texts.value: This is the part nobody can copy. Welcoming and competitive at the same time. The higher belts pull the newer ones up. Everybody has a hand in somebody else’s journey. It’s why people stay for years, and why the ones who move away still call this place home.

texts.value: “I keep the traditional jiu‑jitsu alive, and I’m open-minded enough to bring in the new things that make people better.”

title: about / our story
seoTitle: Our Story | Carlson Gracie New Zealand
seoDescription: Jose Gomes found jiu-jitsu at 16 in Brazil and brought it to a town that had none. The story of Carlson Gracie New Zealand, from one blue belt to a family of academies.

sections.label: Top of page — Our story — It started with one blue belt and no plan

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: One blue belt, a three-month visa, and no plan at all.

texts.label: Heading
texts.value: It started with one blue belt and no plan

texts.label: Body text 2
texts.value: Jose Gomes found jiu-jitsu at 16, back in Brazil. He’d tried karate and capoeira first, and neither one grabbed him. Jiu-jitsu did. What hooked him was that he could roll for real from day one, instead of tapping pads and pretending.

images.label: Photo
images.alt: Jose Gomes rolling with a training partner on the mats at the academy

sections.label: The journey — A long way from home

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: Every belt above blue, Jose earned on these mats.

texts.label: Photo caption
texts.value: He started teaching for one reason. He wanted people to train with.

texts.label: A three-month visa — description
texts.value: New Zealand wasn’t much of a decision. A mate mentioned an island at the bottom of the world you could get into on a three-month visa, and that was enough. Jose landed with barely a word of English and no idea what came next, a gym least of all. He just wanted to see somewhere new, and to keep training while he was there.

texts.label: Teaching from scratch — description
texts.value: There was no jiu-jitsu in Queenstown. None in Central Otago. So Jose started teaching, for one simple reason. He wanted people to train with. He earned his purple, brown and black belts here, flying home for camps and leaning on the odd visiting black belt while he had no coach of his own. Slowly, teaching became coaching. Coaching became a school. The school became a family.

sections.label: Good to know — Questions, answered

texts.label: Can I cancel any time? — question
Can I cancel any time? — answer
texts.value: Yes, and we mean it. No lock-in. Train for a couple of weeks, and if it’s not for you, one phone call sorts it. We’d rather you felt free to give it a proper go.

texts.label: I’ve never done jiu-jitsu. Where do I start? — question
texts.value: I’ve never done jiu-jitsu. Where do I start?

texts.label: Do I need to be fit to start? — question
texts.value: Do I need to be fit to start?

texts.label: Do I need to be fit to start? — answer

texts.label: What should I bring to my first class? — question
texts.value: What should I bring to my first class?

texts.label: What should I bring to my first class? — answer
texts.value: Shorts, a t-shirt, water and a towel. We’ll lend you a clean gi, so there’s nothing to buy before you know you love it.

texts.label: Isn’t it just fighting? Will I get hurt? — question
texts.value: Isn’t it just fighting? Will I get hurt?

texts.label: Isn’t it just fighting? Will I get hurt? — answer
texts.value: It looks like a fight from the outside, but it’s a game of leverage and timing. Leave your ego at the door, come to learn, and it’s safe. In our gym, the higher belts make sure of it.

texts.value: What ages are the kids’ classes?

title: privacy
seoTitle: Privacy Policy | Carlson Gracie New Zealand
seoDescription: How Carlson Gracie New Zealand collects, uses and protects your personal information.

sections.label: Top of page — Legal — Privacy policy

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: The short version: we collect only what we need to run your membership, we guard it, and we never sell it.

sections.label: What we collect

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: Draft for review. Have this checked before launch, and finalise the contact email in the CMS.

texts.label: Body text 2
texts.value: When you enquire, book a trial or become a member, we collect the details you give us: your name, contact details, emergency contact, and any health information you choose to share so we can keep you safe on the mats. For kids’ classes we collect a parent or guardian’s details, not the child’s.

texts.label: Body text 3
texts.value: We use your details to run your membership, tell you about class changes, gradings, seminars and events, and keep our records straight. Payments are handled by our booking and payment providers, and we never see or store your full card details.

texts.label: Body text 4
texts.value: We never sell your information, and we never pass it to anyone outside the academy and the providers who run our booking, payment and email systems.

texts.label: Body text 5
texts.value: We sometimes photograph and film classes, seminars and events for the website and our social channels. If you’d rather stay out of frame, tell any coach and we’ll make sure of it. We always ask before featuring kids.

texts.label: Body text 6
texts.value: Under the Privacy Act 2020 you can ask to see the personal information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. One message sorts any of it.

title: terms
seoTitle: Terms & Conditions | Carlson Gracie New Zealand
seoDescription: The terms of training and membership at Carlson Gracie New Zealand, in plain language.

sections.label: Top of page — Legal — Terms & conditions

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: The terms of training with us, in plain language. No fine-print tricks, because that’s not how we run the room.

sections.label: Membership

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: Draft for review. Have this checked before launch.

texts.label: Body text 2
texts.value: Your membership covers every class on the timetable at your home academy, the seminars we host, and the tutorial library in the members’ app. Memberships are billed weekly through our booking provider.

texts.label: Body text 3
texts.value: You can cancel any time. One phone call or message does it, with no notice period beyond the current billing week and no cancellation fee. If you’re heading away for a stretch, ask us about putting your membership on hold instead.

texts.label: Body text 4
texts.value: Brazilian jiu-jitsu is a contact sport, and you train at your own risk. We keep the room safe: you follow your coaches’ instructions, look after your training partners, and tell us about any injury or health condition that could affect you on the mats. Anyone who trains in a way that puts others at risk will be asked to stop.

texts.label: Body text 5
texts.value: Clean gi or no-gi gear every session, trimmed nails, and no shoes on the mats. If you’re unwell or have a skin infection, stay home and let us know. It protects everyone.

texts.label: Body text 6
texts.value: Kids’ classes are for ages 5 to 12, and a parent or guardian must complete the sign-up. We never teach striking to kids, and parents are always welcome to watch.

texts.label: Body text 7
texts.value: Visitors are welcome at casual and weekly rates. The same safety and hygiene expectations apply, and your first stop on arrival is the coach running the class.

title: training / adults
seoTitle: Adults BJJ, Gi & No-Gi | Carlson Gracie Queenstown
seoDescription: The main adult program at Carlson Gracie New Zealand. Gi and no-gi jiu-jitsu for every level, white belt to black belt, in Queenstown.

sections.label: Top of page — Adults, all levels — Gi and no-gi, every level

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: This is where most of the academy lives. White belts and black belts on the same mat, learning the same thing, pushing each other along. It’s friendly and it’s competitive at the same time, and that mix is the whole magic of the place.

images.label: Photo

sections.label: How a class runs — You learn it by doing it

texts.label: Heading
texts.value: You learn it by doing it

texts.label: Photo caption
texts.value: White belts and black belts on the same mat.

texts.label: Taught in blocks — description
texts.value: We teach in blocks, a few weeks on one position, so you go deep instead of skimming the surface. One idea at a time, until it actually sticks.

texts.label: The same shape, every session — heading
The same shape, every session — description
texts.value: Every class is a warm-up, some technique, drilling, then rolling. You always know what you’re walking into, and you always finish with the real thing.

texts.label: Not learned by watching — description
texts.value: You don’t learn jiu-jitsu by watching it. You learn it by doing it, over and over, with someone who knows more than you.

images.label: Photo
images.alt: A coach demonstrating a gi technique with students on the mats

sections.label: The gi and no-gi

texts.label: The gi — description
texts.value: Grips, control and patience. The traditional kimono, and the deepest technical game.

texts.label: No-gi — description
texts.value: Faster and sweatier, more scrambles. The same art at a different speed.

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: Most people end up doing both and loving them for different reasons. Try one, try the other, and see which one grabs you.

seoTitle: Beginners & Fundamentals BJJ | Carlson Gracie Queenstown
seoDescription: A dedicated beginners class to learn the basics of Brazilian jiu-jitsu properly, at a pace that suits someone brand new. No experience needed.

sections.label: Top of page — Beginners / fundamentals — Your first weeks on the mat

texts.label: Heading
texts.value: Your first weeks on the mat

texts.label: Body text 2
texts.value: This is the front door. A dedicated class to learn the basics properly, at a pace that suits someone brand new, before you step into the all-levels sessions. No experience, no pressure, and nobody expecting you to know a thing.

images.label: Photo
images.alt: Two members practising a standing no-gi drill

sections.label: How it works — The basics, taught properly

texts.label: Photo caption
texts.value: Nobody expecting you to know a thing.

texts.label: Foundations, in blocks — description
texts.value: We teach the fundamentals in blocks, a few weeks on one foundation at a time. Posture, escapes, the handful of core positions everything else is built on. You’ll drill them until they feel natural, and you’ll roll gently and safely while it all sinks in. Get these right and the rest of jiu-jitsu opens up.

texts.label: Who it’s for — description
texts.value: Total beginners, and anyone coming back after a break who wants to sharpen the basics. You don’t need to be fit, flexible or tough. You just need to turn up and be willing to learn.

texts.label: Where it leads — description
texts.value: Once the foundations are there, you’re ready for the all-levels adults classes, and Fabio will make sure you’re set. Most people are surprised how quickly they go from lost to holding their own.

sections.label: Got a shy one? — Perfect

texts.label: Body text
texts.value: We never push a nervous kid to join in before they’re ready. We let them watch, warm up, and come in on their own terms. Nine times out of ten, within a month they’re the one dragging you to class.

texts.label: Body text 2
texts.value: “Within a month, we usually get them wanting to be there. A lot of parents say they never felt that comfortable anywhere else.”
